LESSON: THE INTERDEPENDENCE OF LIFE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living things and their Environment
Topic 2.4: The Interdependence of Life
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Interdependence of Life, part of Living things and their Environment in Grade 9 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: What is the role of living and non-living factors in environments?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print and non-print material to search for information on biotic interrelationships, share findings with peers,

2. investigate the interrelationships between biotic factors of the environment in their locality and discuss the findings with peers (include insects, spiders, lizards, toads, chameleons),

3. use digital or print media to search for more information on the interrelationships between biotic factors of the environment,

4. use print and non-print media to search for information on interrelationships between organisms in Kenya national parks and game reserves,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print and non-print material to search for information on biotic interrelationships, share findings with peers,
2. investigate the interrelationships between biotic factors of the environment in their locality and discuss the findings with peers (include insects, spiders, lizards, toads, chameleons),
3. use digital or print media to search for more information on the interrelationships between biotic factors of the environment,
4. use print and non-print media to search for information on interrelationships between organisms in Kenya national parks and game reserves,
5. discuss the effect of abiotic factors on living organisms,
6. search for information on the effect of

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Interdependence of Life together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: the learner develops a sense of responsibility to the nation while searching for information on interrelationships

between organisms in Kenya’s national parks and game reserves.

• Communication and Collaboration: the learner develops speaking and listening skills as they discuss the role of decomposers in

an ecosystem and their importance in recycling nutrients.

Values:
• Patriotism: the learner develops a love for the country as they search for information on interrelationships between organisms

in Kenya’s national parks and game reserves.

• Peace: the learner shows respect for diversity and heritage as they study the interdependence between living and non-living

components of the environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Environmental Conservation: the learner learns the importance of decomposers as they discusses the role of decomposers in an

ecosystem and their importance in recycling nutrients.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner can link the information on the role of decomposers in an ecosystem to the production of manure in Agriculture.
